item.content:encoded:
Cardiff University is offering a wide range of PhD research studentships and projects across multiple academic disciplines for prospective doctoral researchers.

The university’s current PhD listings feature 100 doctoral opportunities, covering fields including Computer Science, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Medicine, Psychology, Environmental Sciences, Geography, Economics and more.

The opportunities include directly funded and competition-funded research projects, with some positions open to students worldwide. Individual projects have different application deadlines, so applicants should carefully check the requirements and closing date for their selected project.

About Cardiff University PhD Opportunities

The available doctoral projects span a broad range of research areas and are hosted across Cardiff University’s academic schools and research centres.

The listings include opportunities in:

  • Computer Science
  • Biological Sciences
  • Chemistry
  • Engineering
  • Physics and Astronomy
  • Mathematics
  • Medicine
  • Psychology
  • Healthcare Sciences
  • Environmental Sciences
  • Geography
  • Economics
  • Politics and Government
  • Sociology
  • Veterinary Sciences
  • Materials Science
  • Nursing and Health
  • Communication and Media Studies
  • Architecture, Building and Planning
  • Languages, Literature and Culture

The university’s listing also includes specialised research groups such as Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics, Biomedicine, Neuroscience, Molecular Biosciences, Cybersecurity, Privacy and HCC Research, and Organisms and Environment.

Featured Cardiff University PhD Projects

The current listing includes a variety of research projects across different schools.

CyberInvent: Where Cybersecurity Research Meets Real-World Impact

This PhD research project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Computer Science & Informatics.

The project is listed as directly funded and is open to UK students. Applications are accepted throughout the year.

Mapping the Developing Brain

This research project focuses on linking brain structure and function through imaging.

It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is listed as a competition-funded project open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Chronic Pain, Sensory Hypersensitivity and Neurodiversity

This project investigates the relationship between chronic pain, sensory hypersensitivity and neurodiversity.

The project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Pain as Neurobiological Surprise

This research project explores persistent pain using human brain imaging and animal studies.

It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Search for Quantization of Space-Time with Photon Counting Interferometry

This project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Physics and Astronomy.

It is listed as a competition-funded PhD opportunity open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 30 October 2026.

Adaptive Virtual-Reality Exergaming for Physical and Cognitive Health in Older Adults

This research project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Healthcare Sciences.

It is competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Medication Adherence in Young People with First Episode Psychosis

This project is a longitudinal mixed-methods biopsychosocial study examining decision-making and medication adherence among young people experiencing a first episode of psychosis.

It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Healthcare Sciences and is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Mapping Cerebellar Network Dysfunction in Episodic Ataxia

This project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Biosciences and examines cerebellar network dysfunction using human organoids.

It is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

From Multi-OMICs to Mechanism

This Cardiff School of Biosciences project focuses on understanding links between protein turnover and therapy resistance in glioblastoma stem cells.

It is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Gene-Diet Interaction and Psychiatric Risk

This project investigates gene-diet interactions and psychiatric risk, with a focus on FADS2 and dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids.

It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Biosciences and is competition funded and open to students worldwide.

Application deadline: 21 October 2026.

Funding Opportunities

The Cardiff University listing distinguishes between different funding statuses.

The current search page includes categories for:

  • UK students
  • European students excluding the UK
  • Non-European students
  • Self-funded students

Applicants should therefore check the funding status attached to each individual PhD project rather than assuming that every listed doctoral opportunity carries the same funding arrangement.

The current first page also identifies some projects as directly funded and others as competition funded.

Application Deadlines

There is no single deadline covering all the listed PhD projects.

For example, the current listings show:

  • CyberInvent — applications accepted all year round
  • Several Psychology, Healthcare Sciences and Biosciences projects — 21 October 2026
  • Photon-counting interferometry project — 30 October 2026

Applicants should therefore review the individual project page for the latest deadline, eligibility conditions and application procedure.

How to Find a Suitable PhD Project

Prospective applicants can use the Cardiff University PhD studentships and projects listing to search according to several criteria.

The listing provides filters for:

  1. Department
  2. Supervisor
  3. Discipline
  4. Research Group
  5. Funding Status
  6. Keywords

This allows prospective students to narrow the available projects according to their academic interests, preferred supervisor, research field and funding circumstances.

Research Supervisors

The current Cardiff University listing includes a large number of potential PhD supervisors across different schools and disciplines.

The supervisor filter includes academics such as Dr Nitesh Kumar, Dr Mohammad Al-Amri, Prof Pete Burnap, Prof Mara Cercignani, Prof H. Grote, Prof P. Sumner, Dr George Tackley, Dr Yasir Syed and many others.

Applicants should examine the research interests of the supervisor attached to their selected project before applying.

Why Applicants Should Check Individual Projects

The 100 available projects do not all have identical funding arrangements, deadlines or eligibility requirements.

For example, the CyberInvent project is directly funded and accepts applications throughout the year, while several other projects are competition funded and have specific October 2026 deadlines.

Applicants should therefore avoid treating the entire listing as one single scholarship programme.

Instead, they should select a specific research project and review its individual requirements before submitting an application.

Application Portal: Cardiff University PHD Studentships

Conclusion

Cardiff University’s current PhD studentships and projects listing provides prospective doctoral researchers with access to 100 PhD opportunities across a broad range of academic disciplines.

The opportunities cover areas from artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, engineering and physics to healthcare, psychology, biosciences, environmental sciences and other social and scientific disciplines.

Some projects are directly funded, while others are competition funded, and eligibility varies between projects. Several current opportunities are open to students worldwide, while others have more specific funding eligibility.

Interested applicants should use the university’s search filters to identify suitable projects, examine the funding status and deadline of their chosen opportunity, review the supervisor and research topic, and then follow the application instructions for that specific project.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity”, an international human rights award established in 1988 to recognise and support individual or collective grassroots initiatives that contribute to the promotion and protection of human rights.

The prize, awarded by the Prime Minister of the French Government, is open to individual applicants and non-governmental organisations regardless of nationality or borders.

For the 2026 edition, applicants are invited to submit projects focused on protecting the right to asylum and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons.

Five winning projects will share a total grant of €70,000 to support the implementation of their projects. The five winners will also be invited to Paris to attend the official award ceremony and will receive a medal.

The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1).

About the French Republic Human Rights Prize

The French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity” was established in 1988.

The prize is intended to recognise and support grassroots initiatives carried out in France or abroad that contribute to the promotion or protection of human rights.

Applications may be submitted by individuals or organisations, and applicants are not required to be French nationals.

The award is administered through the National Consultative Commission on Human Rights (CNCDH).

2026 Prize Theme

The single theme for the 2026 edition is:

Protecting the Right to Asylum and the Fundamental Rights of Refugees, Asylum Seekers and Displaced Persons

Applicants must submit an action or project that addresses this theme and is intended to be implemented in France or another country.

The 2026 theme focuses on protecting the right to asylum and ensuring that people affected by forced displacement can effectively access their fundamental rights.

Background to the 2026 Theme

The right to asylum provides protection to people who are unable to rely on the protection of their own country.

The right is recognised under international refugee law, including the 1951 Geneva Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol.

The call for applications also refers to Article 14 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which recognises the right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution.

The 2026 call highlights the importance of strengthening legal systems that protect the right to asylum and incorporate international human rights and refugee law into domestic legislation.

The call also notes the scale of forced displacement around the world.

According to figures cited in the call from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), there were 117.3 million forcibly displaced people worldwide at the end of June 2025, including recognised refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced people.

Who Can Submit an Application?

Applications can be submitted by:

  • Individuals
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Organisations implementing human-rights-based projects
  • Applicants of any nationality

The applicant must have a project or action related to guaranteeing the right to asylum and protecting the fundamental rights of people experiencing forced displacement.

Projects may concern refugees covered by the Geneva Convention, asylum seekers whose applications are being examined, or people displaced within their own countries.

What Types of Projects Are Eligible?

The prize is intended for projects based on a human-rights approach that seek to guarantee the right to asylum and fundamental rights.

Particular consideration will be given to projects that:

  • Provide comprehensive support to affected individuals
  • Implement transformative and restorative measures
  • Ensure the active participation of people directly concerned by the project

The projects should focus on rights protection, advocacy, legal support or related activities rather than direct material assistance.

Examples of Eligible Projects

The 2026 call identifies several types of projects that may be considered.

Public Awareness and Advocacy

Projects may raise public awareness about asylum and refugee rights or undertake advocacy directed at public authorities.

Such initiatives could seek to improve understanding of legal protections and promote policies or practices that protect the rights of displaced people.

Legal and Administrative Assistance

Projects may provide legal and administrative assistance to refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced persons.

This may include helping people effectively access rights such as:

  • Residence rights
  • Fair procedures
  • Access to justice
  • Civil and political rights
  • Economic rights
  • Social rights
  • Cultural rights

Projects should be connected to rights guaranteed under applicable international instruments.

Training for Stakeholders

Eligible initiatives may provide training to stakeholders involved in asylum and displacement matters.

Potential participants may include:

  • Border police
  • Government administrations
  • Health services
  • Social services
  • Other professionals involved in asylum procedures

The objective can be to strengthen understanding and implementation of human rights obligations.

Integration, Resettlement and Restoration of Rights

Projects may support the effective exercise of rights associated with integration into host societies.

They may also address resettlement or the restoration of rights for internally displaced people.

Prize and Financial Award

Five projects will be selected as winners.

The five winners will share a total grant of:

€70,000

The grant is allocated by the National Consultative Commission on Human Rights (CNCDH) for implementation of the winning projects.

The five winners will also receive a medal and may refer to themselves as laureates of the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize.

Special Mentions

In addition to the five winners, the next five highest-ranked candidates will receive a Special Mention medal.

The Special Mention is awarded by the Ambassador of France in the recipient’s country of origin.

Special Mention recipients do not receive a financial award.

Prize winners and Special Mention recipients may also benefit from international protection afforded by French diplomacy.

Award Ceremony

The five prize winners will be invited to Paris, France, to attend the official award ceremony.

The 2026 Prize is expected to be formally awarded around 10 December 2026, which is International Human Rights Day.

The award will be presented by the Prime Minister or another Minister of the French Republic.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit a complete application file.

The application must include the following:

1. Letter of Application

Applicants must provide a signed letter of application.

For an NGO, the letter must be submitted and signed by the organisation’s President or legal representative.

Individual applicants must submit and sign their own application letter.

2. Completed Application Form

Applicants must complete the official application form provided with the call for applications.

The form provides detailed information about the activities carried out by the applicant or organisation.

The application form is available through the CNCDH website.

3. Postal and Banking Details

Applicants must provide their postal and banking information.

This includes the relevant RIB/IBAN details of the NGO or individual applicant.

Language of the Application

The application file should be drafted in French.

However, the call states that applications submitted in English or Spanish may be considered at the discretion of the jury.

Applicants who can submit their application in French should follow the stated language requirement.

Application Deadline

The complete application must be submitted no later than:

4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1)

Applications received after the deadline may not be considered.

Applicants should therefore allow sufficient time to complete the application form, prepare supporting information and submit the complete application file.

How to Apply

Applicants should:

  1. Review the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize theme.
  2. Confirm that their project addresses the protection of asylum rights and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers or displaced persons.
  3. Review the official Prize Rules.
  4. Download and complete the official application form.
  5. Prepare the required signed application letter.
  6. Prepare the applicant’s postal and banking details, including RIB/IBAN.
  7. Prepare the application in French, where possible.
  8. Submit the complete application before the deadline.

Applications can be submitted by post or email.

Postal Submission

CNCDH – For the attention of Mrs. Cécile RIOU-BATISTA
20 avenue de Ségur
75007 Paris
France

Email Submission

prixdesdroitsdelhomme@cncdh.fr

Important Application Information

Applicants should carefully review the official Prize Rules before submitting their applications.

The official rules and application information are available through the CNCDH website.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed project is clearly connected to the 2026 theme and focuses on human rights protection rather than direct material assistance.

Conclusion

The 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity” provides an opportunity for individuals and NGOs to gain recognition and financial support for projects protecting the rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons.

The 2026 edition focuses specifically on protecting the right to asylum and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons.

Five selected winners will share €70,000 for the implementation of their projects and will be invited to Paris for the official award ceremony. Five additional candidates will receive Special Mention medals without a financial award.

Eligible applicants should prepare their project information, application letter, official application form and required banking and postal details before submitting their complete application.

The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1).

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications for a 13-month leadership development programme designed for experienced leaders working to strengthen community investment, capital, policy and practice.

Organised by the Center for Community Investment (CCI), the fellowship supports leaders who are already engaged in strategic work that can help build more just and resilient communities, with particular attention to small- and mid-size cities and communities across the South.

The programme combines collaborative problem-solving, personalised coaching, systems thinking, peer learning and in-person seminars to help fellows strengthen their leadership practice and develop actionable strategies for their communities.

Applications close on October 15, 2026.

About the Fulcrum Fellowship

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for established leaders who have significant responsibility within their organisations and are working on challenges where access to capital can contribute to community-level change.

Over the course of 13 months, fellows will participate in a combination of in-person and virtual activities designed to strengthen their ability to develop strategies, collaborate across sectors and use capital more effectively.

The programme creates a cohort of leaders with diverse experiences, sectors, geographies and career paths.

What the Fellowship Offers

Throughout the 13-month programme, fellows participate in:

  • Collaborative problem-solving
  • Personalised leadership coaching
  • Systems-thinking exercises
  • Five multi-day in-person seminars
  • Monthly virtual coaching sessions
  • Group learning sessions
  • Peer networking
  • Leadership development
  • Strategies for community investment and capital deployment

The programme is designed to connect fellows with peers who are addressing complementary challenges in different communities and sectors.

CCI’s Capital Absorption Framework

A central component of the Fulcrum Fellowship is the Center for Community Investment’s Capital Absorption Framework.

Fellows use the framework and related systems-thinking tools to better understand how capital moves through communities and how different structures influence the ability of communities to access and use capital.

Through this work, fellows develop strategies for advancing community-defined priorities and addressing systemic barriers that affect opportunity.

In-Person Seminars

Applicants should be prepared to participate in five in-person seminars in Berkeley, California.

The scheduled seminar dates are:

  • April 13–15, 2027
  • July 13–15, 2027
  • October 26–28, 2027
  • February 1–3, 2028
  • May 2–4, 2028

Participation in these sessions is part of the 13-month fellowship commitment.

Experienced Faculty and Peer Learning

The fellowship is led by experienced faculty and brings together a diverse group of leaders working on community investment and related challenges.

The cohort-based structure gives participants opportunities to learn from other leaders, exchange experiences and test new approaches to leadership and capital strategy.

Fellows can also develop relationships with peers who may continue collaborating beyond the programme.

What Fellows Gain

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed to help participants strengthen their ability to:

  • Move capital toward community-defined priorities
  • Apply systems-thinking approaches to complex challenges
  • Develop stronger leadership strategies
  • Reconsider existing approaches to community investment
  • Work collaboratively across sectors
  • Build relationships with other leaders
  • Strengthen organisational capacity
  • Develop practical strategies for community-level change

Fellows also become part of a network of leaders working to influence the broader community investment ecosystem.

What Organisations Gain

The benefits of the programme extend beyond individual fellows.

Participants can bring new leadership approaches, strategies and relationships back to their organisations.

The programme is intended to help fellows develop sharper strategies, stronger networks and leadership tools that can be applied to their organisations and communities.

Who Can Apply?

The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for experienced leaders with meaningful authority within their organisations and a strong network of colleagues and partners with whom they can work.

Applicants should demonstrate experience and an established commitment to community-focused work.

Eligible applicants should:

Lead Strategic Work

Applicants should be leading strategic work that has meaningful importance to their organisation, community or broader field.

Demonstrate a Commitment to Racial Equity

Applicants should be committed to advancing racial equity and be able to demonstrate tangible results or sustained efforts through their work.

Have Significant Professional Experience

Applicants should have 10 to 15 years of experience working in one of the programme’s focus fields.

These include:

  • Shared ownership
  • Climate resilience
  • Housing and community development
  • Creative placemaking
  • Philanthropy
  • Finance

Be Willing to Rethink Existing Strategies

Fellows should be open to reconsidering and reframing existing strategies in order to accelerate progress and deepen their impact.

Develop Leadership Self-Awareness

Applicants should be interested in developing greater self-awareness and personal effectiveness as leaders.

Participate in Coaching and Peer Learning

Successful fellows should be willing to learn, give and receive coaching and actively participate in a network of diverse peers.

Commit to the Full Programme

Applicants must be able to commit to the entire 13-month programme.

The application also requires written endorsement from the applicant’s organisation.

Information Session

CCI will host an information session for prospective applicants.

Date: September 28, 2026
Time: 1:00 p.m. CT / 2:00 p.m. ET

The session will feature Fulcrum alum and CCI Executive Director Omar Carrillo Tinajero.

Interested applicants can attend to learn more about the fellowship and hear directly from programme leadership and alumni.

Application Deadline

The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 application deadline is:

October 15, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to review the programme requirements and application materials carefully before submitting their applications.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should:

  1. Review the Fulcrum Fellowship programme criteria.
  2. Confirm that their professional experience aligns with the fellowship requirements.
  3. Review the application guide and frequently asked questions.
  4. Discuss the fellowship commitment with their organisation.
  5. Obtain the required organisational endorsement.
  6. Prepare the application materials.
  7. Submit the application before October 15, 2026.

Conclusion

The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 provides an intensive 13-month leadership development experience for experienced community investment leaders working across areas such as housing and community development, climate resilience, finance, philanthropy, shared ownership and creative placemaking.

Through coaching, peer learning, systems thinking and five in-person seminars in Berkeley, California, fellows will have opportunities to strengthen their leadership practice and develop strategies for moving capital toward community-defined priorities.

The fellowship is intended for established leaders with significant professional experience, organisational responsibility and a demonstrated commitment to advancing racial equity and community-level change.

Interested applicants should review the eligibility criteria and prepare their applications before the October 15, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
\The CGBD Research Fellowship by DIFFvelopment offers undergraduate students, graduate students and visionary thinkers from around the world an opportunity to develop research ideas focused on the future and sustainable empowerment of Black communities globally.

The fellowship is designed for emerging researchers and thinkers who want to move beyond conventional approaches and develop bold, solutions-driven research that can contribute to meaningful change across Black communities.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, with applications submitted by 31 July each year considered for the upcoming fellowship cycle beginning in November. Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following fellowship cycle.

About the CGBD Research Fellowship

The CGBD Fellowship is a research-focused initiative run by DIFFvelopment.

According to the programme overview provided, the fellowship seeks to empower young researchers to reimagine the future of the global Black community through bold, solutions-driven research.

Rather than simply focusing on academic research for its own sake, the programme invites participants to develop actionable research plans that can contribute to sustainable empowerment across Black communities globally.

This makes the fellowship relevant to individuals interested in using research, ideas and evidence to explore challenges and opportunities affecting Black communities.

What Is the Purpose of the Fellowship?

The CGBD Research Fellowship is centred on the development of research that can contribute to the long-term empowerment of Black communities.

Participants are expected to think critically about issues affecting Black communities and develop research plans that can potentially contribute to solutions.

The programme’s stated focus includes:

  • Reimagining the future of the global Black community.
  • Developing bold and solutions-driven research.
  • Creating actionable research plans.
  • Supporting sustainable empowerment.
  • Encouraging young researchers and visionary thinkers.
  • Connecting research with issues affecting Black communities globally.

The emphasis on actionable research means applicants should consider not only what problem they want to study, but also how their research can contribute to practical understanding, solutions or positive change.

APPLY HERE

Who Is Invited to Apply?

The programme specifically invites:

  1. Undergraduate students
  2. Graduate students
  3. Visionary thinkers

The opportunity is open to applicants worldwide, according to the programme overview supplied.

This broad eligibility makes the fellowship relevant to people at different stages of their academic and research journeys, as well as thinkers who may have ideas that extend beyond a traditional academic pathway.

What Will Selected Fellows Do?

Selected participants will develop actionable research plans.

This means fellows will be expected to take their research interests or ideas and develop them into structured plans that address issues relevant to sustainable empowerment across Black communities.

The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity to develop research thinking around questions such as:

  • What challenges are affecting Black communities?
  • What evidence is needed to better understand those challenges?
  • What solutions could potentially address identified issues?
  • How can research contribute to sustainable empowerment?
  • How can research findings eventually be translated into practical action?

Applicants should therefore consider how their proposed research can go beyond identifying a problem and contribute toward understanding possible solutions.

A Global Focus on Black Communities

One of the defining characteristics of the CGBD Fellowship is its global perspective.

The programme refers to the global Black community, rather than restricting its focus to one country or region.

This creates room for research examining issues affecting Black communities in different geographical contexts.

Depending on the researcher’s interests, potential areas of inquiry could include issues affecting Black communities across different countries and regions, provided the proposed research aligns with the programme’s stated focus on sustainable empowerment.

The global orientation can also provide an opportunity for applicants to think about similarities and differences between Black communities in different parts of the world.

Solutions-Driven Research

The fellowship places particular emphasis on solutions-driven research.

Solutions-driven research focuses not only on understanding a problem but also on exploring practical approaches that could help address it.

For applicants, this means a strong research concept should clearly communicate:

  • The issue being investigated.
  • Why the issue matters.
  • The community or communities affected.
  • The research questions being considered.
  • What the research aims to discover.
  • How the findings could contribute to solutions.
  • How the research could support sustainable empowerment.

Applicants should therefore approach their proposals with both research and potential impact in mind.

Developing an Actionable Research Plan

A central component of the fellowship is the development of an actionable research plan.

An actionable plan provides a structured pathway for turning an idea into research that can realistically be pursued.

Applicants should think carefully about the relationship between their research problem, objectives and expected outcomes.

A well-developed research concept can help demonstrate that the applicant has thought about how their proposed work could contribute to the broader objectives of the CGBD Fellowship.

Who May Benefit From the Opportunity?

The fellowship can be relevant to students and thinkers interested in a wide range of issues connected to Black communities.

Potential applicants may include people working or studying in areas where research can contribute to community empowerment, social development, education, economics, policy, culture, technology, health, entrepreneurship or other fields.

However, the supplied programme overview does not provide a definitive list of eligible research disciplines. Applicants should therefore consult the full CGBD Fellowship Overview for the programme’s detailed research requirements.

Fellowship Funding and Financial Support

The CGBD Fellowship is explicitly described as an unpaid opportunity.

Applicants should therefore understand that participation does not constitute paid employment and that the programme does not provide a standard fellowship salary based on the information supplied.

However, DIFFvelopment states that fellows who demonstrate financial need may be eligible for a modest technology stipend.

The purpose of this stipend is to support:

  • Internet access
  • Remote participation
  • Technology-related needs associated with participating in the fellowship

The availability of this support is subject to eligibility and demonstrated financial need.

Applicants should not assume that every fellow will automatically receive the technology stipend.

Is the CGBD Fellowship a Paid Opportunity?

No.

The programme overview specifically states that the CGBD Fellowship is unpaid.

However, fellows who demonstrate financial need may be considered for a modest technology stipend to assist with internet access and remote participation.

Therefore, applicants should distinguish between the fellowship itself and the possible technology support.

Application Timeline

The CGBD Fellowship follows a rolling application process.

This means applications are not limited to one fixed application period during the year.

However, there is an important annual consideration date:

Applications submitted by 31 July

Applications received by 31 July each year will be considered for the upcoming CGBD Fellowship cycle beginning in November.

Applications submitted after 31 July

Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following fellowship cycle.

This distinction is important for applicants planning when to submit their applications.

For example, an applicant submitting before the annual 31 July consideration date may be considered for the cycle beginning in November, while an application submitted after that date will generally move into consideration for the subsequent cycle.

Application Deadline

The programme operates on a rolling basis rather than having one permanent annual closing date.

The key annual date stated in the programme information is:

31 July each year — applications submitted by this date are considered for the upcoming fellowship cycle beginning in November.

Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following cycle.

Because the programme operates on this rolling basis, applicants should review the current application information before submitting to confirm which fellowship cycle their application will be considered for.

Visit HERE to learn more about the CGBD Research Fellowship 2026–2027

How to Apply

Applicants interested in the CGBD Research Fellowship should review the programme’s full fellowship overview before applying.

The supplied programme information provides a CGBD Fellowship Overview containing the full programme details:

CGBD Fellowship Overview

The full overview should be consulted for detailed information about the application requirements, research expectations and fellowship process that are not included in the short programme summary provided.

Important Note for Applicants

DIFFvelopment states that it does not engage external recruiters or agencies.

Applicants should therefore be cautious about anyone claiming to represent DIFFvelopment as an external recruiter or agency in connection with the CGBD Fellowship.

Applicants should use the official programme information and application process when seeking to participate.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Programme CGBD Research Fellowship
Organisation DIFFvelopment
Focus Solutions-driven research and sustainable empowerment across Black communities globally
Eligible applicants Undergraduate students, graduate students and visionary thinkers
Geographic scope Worldwide
Compensation Unpaid
Possible support Modest technology stipend for fellows demonstrating financial need

item.content:encoded:
The Chatham House Africa Programme is inviting applications for a Research Fellow (West Africa) to contribute to independent policy research and convening activities focused on West Africa, with significant work on Nigeria and scope to expand regional coverage over time.

This is a full-time, permanent position based in London, offering an annual salary of £45,000. The successful candidate will join Chatham House’s Africa Programme and contribute to research covering governance, politics, economy and trade, security, and the wider regional and international relationships of African states.

The application deadline is Tuesday, 29 September 2026 at 23:59 BST.

About the Chatham House Africa Programme

The Africa Programme conducts policy research examining issues affecting individual African states as well as their regional and international relations. The programme seeks to produce research that is relevant to policymakers and contributes to discussions on major political, economic, governance and security issues affecting the continent.

As a Research Fellow, the successful applicant will contribute to this work through research projects, publications, stakeholder engagement, events and conferences.

The position is particularly focused on West Africa, including substantial work on Nigeria, while also providing an opportunity for the researcher to expand their regional coverage over time.

The role therefore combines academic and policy-oriented research with practical engagement with stakeholders and the wider policy community.

Research Fellow (West Africa) Role Overview

The Research Fellow will be expected to contribute to the development and delivery of a range of research and convening activities relating to West Africa.

The position covers several major thematic areas, including:

  • Politics and governance
  • Economy and trade
  • Security
  • Regional affairs
  • International relations
  • Policy research and analysis

The successful candidate will also contribute to significant research work concerning Nigeria and will have the opportunity to work across different issues affecting West Africa.

This makes the position suitable for an experienced researcher who can work across multiple policy areas rather than focusing exclusively on one narrow research topic.

Key Responsibilities

1. Designing and Delivering Research Projects

A major responsibility of the Research Fellow will be to help develop and deliver research projects that support the strategic objectives of the Africa Programme and Chatham House.

This includes contributing to research from the initial development stage through to the production and dissemination of findings.

The successful candidate will therefore need to be capable of identifying important research questions, developing research proposals and contributing to projects that have clear policy relevance.

Research projects will be expected to advance understanding of important developments in West Africa and generate findings that can contribute to policy discussions.

2. Producing Policy-Relevant Research

The Research Fellow will produce high-quality research relating to West Africa.

The position specifically covers research across areas such as:

  • Politics
  • Governance
  • Economy
  • Trade
  • Security

The role requires more than simply producing academic research. The research should be policy relevant, meaning that the findings should be useful to people involved in understanding, developing or implementing policy.

The researcher will therefore need to demonstrate the ability to analyse complex issues, identify important developments and communicate findings clearly to a policy audience.

3. Research on Nigeria and West Africa

The role includes significant work on Nigeria, alongside broader research covering West Africa.

Nigeria is one of the major areas of focus mentioned in the position, meaning applicants should be prepared to engage deeply with developments affecting the country while also understanding the wider regional context.

The position also provides scope for the successful researcher to expand their regional coverage over time.

This means the role can involve developing expertise beyond an initial area of specialization as the researcher contributes to the broader work of the Africa Programme.

4. Developing Research Proposals

The successful candidate will be expected to have experience developing successful research proposals.

This is an important requirement because research at a policy institute often begins with identifying a relevant issue, developing a research question, establishing an appropriate research approach and presenting a convincing proposal.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate previous experience turning research ideas into structured and deliverable research projects.

5. Supporting Research Events and Conferences

The role is not limited to written research.

The Research Fellow will also be involved in designing and supporting research events and conferences.

These activities are intended to maximise the diversity of voices, expertise and perspectives involved in discussions about West Africa.

Responsibilities may therefore involve helping to develop event content, identify relevant participants and support discussions that bring together different perspectives and areas of expertise.

Skills and Experience Required

Chatham House is looking for an individual with a significant track record of policy research on West Africa.

Experience in West African Policy Research

Applicants should have substantial experience conducting policy research relating to West Africa.

This should demonstrate an understanding of important regional issues and the ability to produce research that can contribute to policy discussions.

Experience developing successful research proposals is also specifically highlighted as a requirement.

Strong Analytical Skills

The role requires exceptional analytical ability.

The successful candidate will need to examine complex political, economic, governance and security issues, identify important information and develop clear conclusions that can be communicated to policy audiences.

Strong analytical skills are particularly important because the position covers multiple thematic areas across the region.

Excellent Writing and Communication Skills

The successful candidate will also need exceptional writing and communication skills.

This includes the ability to produce high-quality policy-relevant publications and communicate research findings effectively.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate a background in publications that have had demonstrable impact.

This indicates that Chatham House is looking for someone with an established record of communicating research beyond simply completing internal research assignments.

Ability to Manage Multiple Priorities

The Research Fellow will work across research projects, events, stakeholder engagement and other programme activities.

Applicants therefore need experience managing multiple priorities while maintaining a high standard of work.

The ability to deliver high-quality work within deadlines is specifically identified in the requirements.

What Kind of Researcher Is Chatham House Looking For?

The advertised position is aimed at an experienced policy researcher rather than someone entering research for the first time.

The successful applicant is expected to bring:

  1. A significant track record of research on West Africa.
  2. Experience developing successful research proposals.
  3. Strong analytical skills.
  4. Excellent writing and communication abilities.
  5. Experience producing policy-relevant publications.
  6. Evidence that their research has had demonstrable impact.
  7. The ability to manage several priorities simultaneously.
  8. The ability to consistently deliver high-quality work within deadlines.
  9. An understanding of political, governance, economic, trade and security issues affecting West Africa.

Employment Details

The position offers the following employment conditions:

Detail Information
Position Research Fellow (West Africa)
Programme Africa Programme
Organisation Chatham House
Contract Full-time, permanent
Salary £45,000 per year
Location St James’s Square, London
Working arrangement Hybrid
Office requirement At least 2 days per week onsite
Remote-only work Not available
Application deadline 29 September 2026, 23:59 BST

Although the position is described as hybrid, applicants should note that this is not a fully remote position.

The successful candidate will be expected to work onsite at the London office for at least two days each week. Additional flexibility may also be required depending on event requirements.

Salary and Benefits

The advertised salary is £45,000 per year.

In addition to the salary, Chatham House lists a range of employment benefits.

Annual Leave

Benefits include approximately 37 days of annual leave, including public holidays and Chatham House closure days.

Pension

Employees can access a pension salary exchange arrangement.

Employee Assistance

The organisation provides an employee assistance programme as part of its employee benefits.

Parental Leave

Parental leave is also included among the benefits offered to employees.

Flexible Working

The position provides flexible working arrangements, although this should not be interpreted as fully remote employment because the role has a minimum requirement for onsite work in London.

Chatham House also states that it offers other benefits intended to support employees’ individual lifestyles and working needs.

Workplace and Equal Opportunity

Chatham House states that it is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity.

The organisation says it does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics and encourages applications from people from all backgrounds.

Applicants who require support or adjustments during the application experience can contact the Human Resources team at HR@Chathamhouse.org.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Research Fellow (West Africa) at Chatham House

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to experienced researchers with established expertise in West Africa.

The advertised requirements indicate that applicants should have a substantial policy research track record rather than simply an academic interest in the region.

Potential applicants should be able to demonstrate experience in:

  • West African policy research
  • Research proposal development
  • Policy-relevant publications
  • Research analysis
  • Research communication
  • Managing multiple research priorities
  • Delivering projects within deadlines
  • Producing research with demonstrable impact

Because the role focuses significantly on Nigeria and broader West Africa, applicants should have relevant regional expertise.

Geographic Eligibility

The provided vacancy information does not specify a nationality or citizenship restriction.

It describes the role as a position based at Chatham House’s London office and states that the successful candidate must work onsite at least two days per week.

Therefore, the source information does not establish that the position is restricted to applicants from a particular African country, European country, continent or racial/ethnic background.

Applicants who require specific UK work authorization should check the full vacancy information and relevant employment requirements before applying, as the provided description does not specify the visa or work-permission arrangements.

Race and Ethnicity Eligibility

The vacancy does not specify a particular race or ethnic group as an eligibility requirement.

Instead, Chatham House states that it is an equal opportunity employer, values diversity and encourages applications from all backgrounds.

Why the Role Is Relevant to West Africa

The Research Fellow position provides an opportunity to work on issues that affect both individual countries and the wider region.

Its thematic scope includes governance, politics, economy and trade, and security, allowing the researcher to examine West African issues from multiple policy perspectives.

The role’s significant focus on Nigeria also provides an opportunity for the successful candidate to contribute to research concerning one of the region’s major countries while maintaining a broader West African focus.

The stated possibility of expanding regional coverage over time also means that the position is not limited to one country or one narrowly defined policy issue.

APPY HERE

Application Deadline

Applicants must submit their applications by:

Tuesday, 29 September 2026 at 23:59 BST.

Candidates interested in the position should allow sufficient time to review the complete job description and prepare their application before the closing time.

How to Apply

The full job description and application process are available through the Chatham House careers portal.

Full Job Description and Application:
Chatham House – Research Fellow (West Africa)

Applicants should review the complete vacancy information carefully because the information provided above is based on the opportunity details supplied for this article.

Conclusion

The Research Fellow (West Africa) position at Chatham House is a full-time, permanent research opportunity focused on policy research concerning West Africa, with significant work on Nigeria.

The successful candidate will contribute to research projects, policy-relevant publications, stakeholder engagement, research events and conferences across areas including politics, governance, economy and trade, and security.

Chatham House is seeking a researcher with a significant track record in West African policy research, experience developing successful research proposals, strong analytical and communication skills, evidence of impactful policy publications and the ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines.

The role is based in London, operates on a hybrid basis and requires at least two days of onsite work each week. It offers a salary of £45,000 per year, alongside approximately 37 days of annual leave and other employment benefits.

Interested applicants should ensure they meet the experience requirements and review the complete vacancy before applying.

item.content:encoded:
The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 are now open to eligible doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa seeking financial support to undertake a short research stay at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country.

Supported by the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (AvH), the programme is designed to strengthen scientific capacity, research collaboration, networking, and knowledge exchange among young researchers across sub-Saharan Africa.

The grants enable eligible doctoral candidates to spend one to two months at a host university or research institution in another sub-Saharan African country while working with an experienced scientific host. The research stay must contribute directly to the applicant’s doctoral research.

For the 2026 call, applications must be submitted in English by 16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT.

What Are the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants?

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants are research mobility opportunities designed to support junior researchers pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa.

The programme allows doctoral candidates to temporarily move to another sub-Saharan African country to undertake research activities that cannot be conducted in their home country.

During the research stay, the researcher works with an identified scientific host at a university or research institute.

The programme aims to strengthen:

  • Scientific research capacity
  • Research collaboration between African institutions
  • Professional networks among young researchers
  • International scientific networking
  • Knowledge and skills transfer
  • Collaboration between doctoral researchers and experienced researchers
  • Research that contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries

The programme is supported financially by BMZ and with support from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation.

Two AGNES Mobility Grant Programmes

The 2026 call provides two different mobility grant opportunities.

1. General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant

The General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is generally open to both male and female candidates.

Eligible male and female doctoral researchers can apply for this grant provided they meet the programme requirements.

2. Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant

The Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is specifically for female candidates.

Female researchers may apply for either the General Grant, the Special Grant, or both.

However, a female applicant can receive a maximum of one grant.

Male candidates are only eligible to apply for the General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant.

AGNES also encourages applications from researchers across a wide range of disciplines, including:

  • Sciences
  • Humanities
  • Law
  • Social Sciences

No Geographical Quota

The 2026 call states that there is no geographical quota for AGNES grants within sub-Saharan Africa.

This means eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply.

However, AGNES specifically welcomes applications from eligible candidates from countries described in the call as under-represented.

These include:

  • Burkina Faso
  • Ghana
  • Guinea
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Liberia
  • Mali
  • Senegal
  • Sierra Leone
  • Angola
  • Central African Republic
  • Chad
  • Congo Brazzaville
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Equatorial Guinea
  • Gabon
  • Rwanda
  • Zambia
  • Uganda
  • Tanzania
  • Malawi
  • Lesotho
  • Botswana
  • Mozambique
  • Mauritius
  • Mauritania
  • Namibia
  • Zimbabwe
  • Cape Verde
  • Sao Tome and Principe

Importantly, being from one of these countries is not presented as an exclusive eligibility requirement. The call states that all eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply.

What Does the Grant Support?

The AGNES Mobility Grant enables a doctoral researcher to undertake a research stay lasting between one and two months at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country.

The proposed research must form part of the applicant’s doctoral research.

Eligible activities may include:

  • Laboratory research
  • Bench work
  • Research studies
  • Library research
  • Data or other research activities
  • Writing part of the doctoral thesis
  • Other activities directly related to the doctoral research

The proposed research should contribute meaningfully to the applicant’s doctoral work.

The applicant must also demonstrate why the research is relevant to the further development of their home country or other sub-Saharan African countries.

Research Must Not Be Possible in the Home Country

One of the important conditions is that the proposed research activity cannot be conducted in the applicant’s home country.

Applicants therefore need to demonstrate why the host institution provides research facilities, expertise, resources, or other conditions that are unavailable in the applicant’s home country.

This is an important consideration when preparing the research proposal.

Financial Support

The AGNES grant is intended to be financially comprehensive for the short research stay as far as reasonably possible.

The grant can support expenses associated with:

  • Travel
  • Subsistence
  • Research-related expenses
  • Host institution research costs, where applicable

The maximum grant depends on the length of the research stay.

Maximum Grant Amounts

Research Stay Maximum Grant
1 month €2,300
1.5 months €2,650
2 months €3,000

These amounts represent the maximum overall budget, including the host fee.

Research Allowance for the Host Institution

A portion of the grant may be allocated to research costs at the host institution.

The call specifies the following deductions from the total grant:

  • Humanities and Social Sciences: €100 per month
  • Natural and Life Sciences and Engineering Sciences: €200 per month

The scientific host and host institution must request the relevant research cost allowance as part of the required documentation.

Travel Support

Applicants must provide two travel quotations for their journey.

The quotes should cover return travel between:

  • The applicant’s country of residence; and
  • The country where the host institution is located.

Travel may be by:

  • Land transportation; or
  • Economy-class flight

Applicants should therefore research the expected cost of their return journey before submitting the application.

Cost of Living

Applicants must also provide an estimate of their expected cost of living during the research stay.

This should take into account expenses such as:

  • Accommodation or rent
  • Meals
  • Local transportation
  • Health insurance

Applicants are expected to obtain valid health insurance for the duration of their research stay.

The scientific host and host institution are expected to assist applicants in finding affordable accommodation and preparing realistic subsistence estimates.

APPLY HERE

Who Can Apply?

The programme is specifically aimed at junior researchers who are currently pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa.

Applicants must meet several eligibility requirements.

1. Must Be a Doctoral Student

The applicant must be officially registered for a doctoral degree at a university or tertiary institution in sub-Saharan Africa at the time of application.

Current doctoral students are eligible.

The call specifically states that applicants must provide official proof of registration for their postgraduate degree.

2. Must Be a National of a Sub-Saharan African Country

Applicants must be nationals of a sub-Saharan African country.

The programme therefore focuses specifically on researchers from sub-Saharan Africa.

3. Must Have at Least One Published Research Article

Applicants must have at least one published article from their thesis work.

The article must have been published in a non-predatory journal.

The call specifies that only journals indexed by:

  • SCOPUS, or
  • Web of Science

will be considered.

Applicants therefore need to provide evidence that their publication meets these requirements.

4. Research Must Be Relevant to Development

The applicant must clearly demonstrate how their research contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries.

The proposal should therefore explain the broader relevance and potential development contribution of the research.

5. Research Must Require the Host Institution

The applicant must demonstrate that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country.

This requirement helps ensure that the mobility component of the grant is necessary for the proposed research.

6. Identified Scientific Host Required

Applicants must already have an identified scientific host.

The applicant and scientific host must agree on:

  • The research proposal
  • The research activities
  • The work schedule
  • The timing of the research stay

Applications without an identified scientific host and mutually agreed proposal/work schedule will not be considered.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit a complete application containing all required documents.

The maximum total application size is 12 MB.

1. Research or Project Proposal

Applicants must prepare a short research/project proposal.

The proposal:

  • Must be written in English.
  • Must not exceed five pages.
  • Must outline the proposed research activity.
  • Must explain the research objectives.
  • Must include a work schedule.
  • Must explain how the research will be undertaken at the host institution.

The scientific host must agree in writing to the proposal and proposed schedule.

2. Standard CV

Applicants must submit a standard CV using the AGNES CV template.

The CV must be written in English.

The official 2026 AGNES Mobility CV template is provided as part of the application information.

3. Proof of Doctoral Registration

Applicants must provide official proof that they are currently registered for their doctoral degree.

This is an important requirement because the programme is specifically intended for current doctoral students.

4. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit official academic transcripts showing grades obtained during:

  • Undergraduate studies
  • Postgraduate studies, where applicable

If the transcript is written in a language other than English, applicants must also provide an official explanation of the grading system in English.

5. List of Publications

Applicants must provide a list of their published articles in eligible non-predatory journals.

The publication list must include SCOPUS or Web of Science links for each publication.

Applicants must also include an electronic copy of the first page of each publication showing:

  • Article title
  • Authors
  • Abstract

The publication list and first pages of the publications must be combined into one PDF document.

The document should begin with a descriptive title, such as:

“LIST OF PUBLICATIONS FOR [APPLICANT’S NAME]”

The publication list should then be followed by the first page of each publication.

6. Travel Quotations

Applicants must provide two travel quotations for return travel between their country of residence and the host institution’s country.

The quotes can cover:

  • Land travel; or
  • Economy-class air travel

7. Estimated Cost of Living

Applicants must provide an estimated budget for their stay.

The estimate should cover:

  • Rent/accommodation
  • Meals
  • Local transportation
  • Health insurance

8. Letter of Invitation From the Scientific Host

The scientific host must provide a letter of invitation written in English.

The letter must:

  1. Confirm that a place to work will be available during the proposed research period.
  2. Include a binding declaration from the host institution requesting the relevant research cost allowance.

The host institution should therefore be involved in the preparation of the application rather than being contacted only after the application is submitted.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants 2026

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted online using the application form provided by AGNES.

The application form is:

https://forms.gle/t57E7k9gTTtd7R7XA

Applicants should carefully check their application before submitting it.

The call specifically warns that applications that:

  • Do not follow the stated guidelines; or
  • Are missing required documents

will be automatically rejected.

Applicants should therefore make sure that all required documents are complete, correctly formatted, written in the required language, and included before submission.

Application Language

All applications must be submitted in English.

This applies particularly to the research proposal, CV, scientific host invitation letter, and other documents where English is specifically required.

Applicants whose academic transcripts use another language must provide the required official explanation of the grading system in English.

Grant Acceptance and Reporting Requirements

The grant is a once-off award and cannot be used to finance research stays retrospectively.

If selected, both the grant recipient and the scientific host must provide:

  • A signed letter of acceptance
  • A contractual agreement

These documents must be emailed to the AGNES Governing Board within two weeks of receiving the offer, according to the call information.

Following completion of the research stay, both the grantee and scientific host are expected to report to AGNES on the progress and success of their collaboration.

This report is expected within six months after completion of the research stay.

Research Stay Timeline

The selection meeting is scheduled for December 2026.

Only selected candidates will be notified.

The earliest possible start date for research stays is:

1 March 2027

Research stays must be completed by:

31 July 2027

Applicants should therefore consider these dates when discussing the proposed research schedule with their scientific host.

Important Dates

Stage Date
Application deadline 16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT
Selection meeting December 2026
Earliest research stay commencement 1 March 2027
Latest completion of research stay 31 July 2027

Key Points Applicants Should Understand

Before applying, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the following requirements:

  1. You must currently be registered for a doctoral degree.
  2. You must be a national of a sub-Saharan African country.
  3. You must have at least one thesis-related article published in an eligible journal.
  4. The journal must be indexed by SCOPUS or Web of Science.
  5. You must identify a scientific host in another sub-Saharan African country.
  6. Your host must agree to your proposal and work schedule.
  7. The proposed research must contribute to your doctoral research.
  8. The research must be relevant to development in sub-Saharan Africa.
  9. The research activity must not be possible in your home country.
  10. Your proposal must be written in English and must not exceed five pages.
  11. Your CV must use the AGNES template.
  12. You must provide academic transcripts.
  13. You must provide evidence of your eligible publications.
  14. You must provide two travel quotations.
  15. You must provide an estimated cost of living.
  16. You must provide a scientific host invitation letter.
  17. The complete application must be submitted online before the deadline.
  18. Missing documents or failure to follow the guidelines can result in automatic rejection.

Why the Programme Matters

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is structured around more than simply providing funding for a short research trip.

The programme aims to strengthen research connections within Africa by allowing doctoral researchers to work with institutions and experienced researchers in other sub-Saharan African countries.

This creates opportunities for researchers to gain access to expertise, facilities, research environments, and professional networks that may not be available at their home institutions.

The programme also places emphasis on research that can contribute to the development of sub-Saharan African countries, meaning applicants are expected to demonstrate the wider relevance of their doctoral research.

The involvement of scientific hosts also creates an opportunity for longer-term professional and research collaboration.

Conclusion

The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 provide doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa with an opportunity to undertake a one- to two-month research stay at another African university or research institution.

With grants of up to €3,000, the programme can contribute toward travel, subsistence, and research-related costs while giving researchers an opportunity to collaborate with experienced scientists and strengthen their professional networks.

The programme is open across academic disciplines, including Sciences, Humanities, Law, and Social Sciences, while the Special AGNES Mobility Grant provides an additional application route specifically for female researchers.

However, applicants must meet several specific requirements, particularly being current doctoral students, having at least one eligible published thesis-related article, identifying a scientific host, and demonstrating that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country.

Interested researchers should begin preparing their research proposal, publication evidence, host invitation, travel quotations, transcripts, and other required documents well before the deadline.
