item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Activate U.S. Fellowship Cohort 2027, an opportunity designed for scientists, engineers, and technology professionals who are ready to move a promising hard-tech innovation from research and development toward commercialization.

The Activate Fellowship is built specifically for technical founders developing hardware-based technologies in areas connected to the physical sciences, biological sciences, and related engineering disciplines. Rather than focusing only on business development, the fellowship provides financial support, entrepreneurship education, mentorship, professional development, community programming, and resources intended to help technical leaders build companies around transformative technologies.

For the 2027 U.S. cohort, applications will close on October 30 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

What Is the Activate Fellowship?

The Activate Fellowship supports scientists, engineers, and technology leaders who are developing technologies with the potential to create significant real-world impact.

The program is particularly focused on hard tech, meaning technologies that require substantial scientific, engineering, research, development, and commercialization work. Fellows are expected to have deep technical knowledge of the technology they are developing and to be capable of leading the technical work required to reduce the risks associated with bringing that technology to market.

The fellowship is designed for people who are transitioning from technical expertise into company leadership and commercialization.

This means applicants do not necessarily need to already be experienced entrepreneurs. In fact, Activate specifically states that fellows should be commercially developing a hardware-based technology for the first time and should not be repeat hard-tech founders.

The program is intended to help bridge the gap between scientific or engineering innovation and the creation of commercially viable technologies.

Activate Fellowship 2027 Benefits

The fellowship provides substantial financial and professional support to selected fellows.

1. $100,000 Annual Living Stipend

Fellows receive a $100,000 living stipend per year.

This financial support is intended to help fellows dedicate themselves to their proposed project or company on a full-time basis.

2. $100,000 in R&D Support

The fellowship also provides $100,000 in research and development support.

This is particularly important for hard-tech founders because developing physical technologies can require significant resources for experimentation, prototyping, testing, technical development, and other R&D activities.

3. $12,000 for Travel and Professional Development

Fellows receive $12,000 per year for travel and professional development.

This can support activities that help fellows expand their technical and professional networks and continue developing their leadership and entrepreneurial capabilities.

4. Health Insurance Stipend

The fellowship provides a health insurance stipend, adding another form of financial support for fellows as they dedicate themselves to their projects.

5. Relocation Allowance

A relocation allowance is also included among the fellowship benefits.

This can help fellows manage relocation-related expenses associated with participating in the program.

Community and Collaboration

The Activate Fellowship is not only a financial support program. Community participation is an important part of the fellowship experience.

Fellows participate in community-based programming every two weeks, including:

  • Workshops
  • Fellow talks
  • Networking opportunities
  • Collaborative activities
  • Professional development opportunities

The program also facilitates what Activate describes as “Collisions”, which are opportunities for fellows to connect with inspiring people, expand their networks, and develop unexpected professional relationships.

Activate emphasizes a community culture that prioritizes people and authentic relationships.

The organization highlights principles such as putting people before the company and being genuine even when difficult situations arise.

This community environment is intended to give fellows access to peers and experienced individuals who can provide perspectives, connections, and support throughout their entrepreneurial journey.

Entrepreneurship Education and Support

Scientists and engineers may have extensive technical expertise but limited experience with entrepreneurship, commercialization, company building, or business leadership.

The Activate Fellowship provides education specifically designed to help address this transition.

Elements of Entrepreneurship

Fellows receive education tailored to the needs of the scientist-turned-founder.

During the first quarter, fellows participate in a weekly Elements of Entrepreneurship course designed to help them develop the business and leadership knowledge needed to commercialize their technology.

One-on-One Mentorship

Fellows receive regular one-on-one mentorship with their community’s Managing Director.

These sessions can be used to work through challenges, evaluate strategies, and refine the direction of the company or proposed project.

Quarterly Advisory Meetings

The fellowship also provides quarterly advisory meetings that function similarly to board meetings.

These meetings are intended to help fellows focus on the most important issues facing their companies and projects.

Personal Development

Activate also places emphasis on the individual fellow rather than focusing exclusively on the company.

Annual retreats and reunions are designed to support fellows’ personal development and provide opportunities for continued connection within the Activate community.

Who Is Eligible for the Activate Fellowship?

Applicants must satisfy specific requirements relating to their education, technical experience, entrepreneurial stage, work authorization, and commitment to their proposed project.

Bachelor’s Degree Requirement

Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree.

Scientific, Engineering, or Technology Experience

Applicants must have at least four years of post-baccalaureate experience in:

  • Scientific research
  • Engineering
  • Technology development

This means the fellowship is intended for individuals who have already developed substantial technical experience beyond their undergraduate education.

First-Time Hard-Tech Founder

Applicants must be leading the commercial development of a hardware-based technology innovation for the first time if awarded the fellowship.

In other words, the program is not designed for repeat hard-tech founders.

The applicant should be moving toward commercializing a hard-tech innovation and taking on a leadership role in the proposed company or project.

Full-Time Commitment

Selected fellows must be prepared to commit full-time to their proposed project or company.

Activate notes that applicants do not necessarily have to have already left their current job or incorporated their company when applying.

The fellowship is designed in part to help enable that transition.

U.S. Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship.

This is an important requirement for applicants who are currently outside the United States or who do not currently have U.S. work authorization.

English Communication

Applicants must be able to communicate proficiently in English.

This is important because fellows participate in entrepreneurship education, mentorship, community programming, networking, and other activities that require effective communication.

Project Eligibility

In addition to meeting the individual fellow requirements, the proposed technology must meet Activate’s project eligibility requirements.

Technology Must Be Based in Relevant Scientific or Engineering Fields

The proposed project must be based in:

  • Physical sciences
  • Biological sciences
  • Related engineering disciplines

The program therefore focuses on technology that has a substantial scientific or engineering foundation.

Technology Must Still Be in Development

The project must still be in development at the application deadline.

It must not yet be ready for full-scale product sales.

This requirement reflects the fellowship’s focus on helping technical innovations move through development and toward commercialization.

Funding Limit

At the time of the application deadline, the proposed project must not have raised more than $2 million in debt or equity funding from non-governmental sources.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider the amount and type of funding their project has already received when determining eligibility.

What Activate Looks For in Fellows

Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not automatically mean that an applicant will be selected.

Activate describes several characteristics it looks for when evaluating potential fellows.

1. Hard-Tech Leadership

Activate wants applicants who can demonstrate leadership in developing transformative technologies.

The ideal applicant should have a strong understanding of the technology they are proposing and be capable of independently leading the technical work involved.

2. Technical Expertise

Applicants should have substantial technical knowledge in the field of their proposed project.

They should be able to:

  • Understand the technical challenges facing their technology
  • Lead technical development
  • Conduct or oversee research and development
  • Reduce technical risks
  • Explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences

Activate notes that many successful applicants have completed PhDs or postdoctoral training.

However, a PhD or postdoctoral background is not presented as an absolute requirement. Activate also welcomes people with technical or R&D experience in industry or equivalent backgrounds.

3. Proof of Concept or Prototype

Activate indicates that many successful applicants have already established an early proof of concept or prototype supported by experimental data demonstrating that their innovation works.

This suggests that applicants should be able to provide evidence supporting the technical feasibility of their proposed innovation.

The technology does not need to be ready for full-scale sales, but applicants should be able to demonstrate meaningful progress in development.

4. Transformative Potential

Activate is interested in technologies that could make a significant difference in the world.

The program looks beyond incremental improvements and asks applicants to consider the potential long-term impact of their technology.

Applicants should be able to explain what the world could look like if their technology were successfully developed and implemented at scale.

5. Leadership Readiness

Activate also looks for applicants who are ready to develop beyond their technical expertise and grow as business leaders.

Applicants should demonstrate the ability or potential to:

  • Lead a company
  • Manage conflict
  • Operate in uncertain situations
  • Act with integrity
  • Mobilize resources
  • Make important decisions
  • Work toward commercialization

The applicant should have a leadership role in the proposed company or project.

6. High Potential Impact of the Fellowship

Activate emphasizes additionality in its selection process.

This means the organization wants to understand whether receiving the fellowship would meaningfully accelerate the applicant’s professional development and the progress of their proposed project.

Applicants should therefore be able to explain why the Activate Fellowship is important at this particular stage of their journey.

A strong application should make clear how the fellowship’s financial support, mentorship, education, community, and resources could change the trajectory of the technology and the applicant’s development as a leader.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Activate Fellowship may be relevant for technical professionals who are moving from research or engineering into commercialization.

Potential applicants may include:

  • Scientists developing a new technology
  • Engineers working on hardware-based innovations
  • Researchers transitioning toward entrepreneurship
  • Technology developers with substantial R&D experience
  • Industry professionals developing a transformative technology
  • Technical experts preparing to commercialize a prototype
  • Scientists or engineers preparing to become first-time hard-tech founders

Applicants should have a strong technical foundation and a project that fits Activate’s hard-tech focus.

APPLY HERE

Application Process

Applicants should follow the application instructions provided by Activate.

The application page states that applicants should first click the “Apply for US Cohort 2027” button and complete the application interest form to receive the link to begin the application.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed project clearly demonstrates:

  1. The scientific or engineering basis of the technology.
  2. The problem the technology is intended to address.
  3. The current development stage.
  4. Evidence that the technology works, where applicable.
  5. The potential impact of the technology.
  6. Their technical expertise and experience.
  7. Their leadership role in the project.
  8. Their plans for commercial development.
  9. Why the Activate Fellowship would significantly accelerate the project.
  10. Their ability to commit to the fellowship full-time if selected.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Activate Fellowship 2027

Application Deadline

Applications for the Activate U.S. Fellowship Cohort 2027 will close on:

October 30 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

Applicants should submit their application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Before starting an application, prospective applicants should carefully assess both their own eligibility and the eligibility of their proposed technology.

In particular, applicants should confirm that they:

  • Have a bachelor’s degree.
  • Have at least four years of post-baccalaureate scientific research, engineering, or technology development experience.
  • Are developing a hardware-based technology.
  • Are commercializing the technology for the first time.
  • Can commit full-time to the proposed project if selected.
  • Are legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship.
  • Can communicate proficiently in English.
  • Have a project based in the physical sciences, biological sciences, or related engineering disciplines.
  • Have not reached full-scale product sales.
  • Have not raised more than $2 million in non-governmental debt or equity funding.

Applicants should also consider whether they can clearly demonstrate the technical expertise, leadership potential, transformative impact, and development progress that Activate looks for in its fellows.

Conclusion

The Activate Fellowship 2027 is designed to help experienced scientists, engineers, and technology developers transition from technical innovation into hard-tech entrepreneurship and commercialization.

Selected fellows receive significant financial support, including a $100,000 annual living stipend, $100,000 in R&D support, $12,000 in annual travel and professional development funds, a health insurance stipend, and a relocation allowance. Beyond financial assistance, the program provides entrepreneurship education, mentorship, advisory support, community programming, networking, and personal development opportunities.

The fellowship is particularly focused on first-time hard-tech founders who have substantial scientific, engineering, or technology development experience and are working on technologies that are still in development.

For applicants who meet the eligibility requirements and are developing a potentially transformative technology, the program provides a structured environment for developing both the technology and the leadership skills needed to take it toward commercialization.

item.content:encoded:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is offering a Solutions Architect Intern opportunity for students interested in cloud computing, software development, machine learning, analytics, security, DevOps, and related technical fields.

The internship is a 12-week, full-time program based in Dallas, Texas, or Seattle, Washington, where interns will receive AWS technical training, mentorship, and hands-on experience working on real customer and business challenges.

Opportunity Overview

  • Position: Solutions Architect Intern, AWSI – 2027
  • Company: Amazon Web Services, Inc.
  • Job ID: 10550494
  • Location: Dallas, TX or Seattle, WA
  • Duration: 12 consecutive weeks
  • Work Schedule: Full-time, up to 40 hours per week
  • Program Format: Cohort-based
  • Tentative Start Dates: May 24 or June 21
  • Degree Level: Bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Expected Graduation: December 2027 – September 2028

About the Amazon Solutions Architect Internship

The Solutions Architect Intern role is designed for students who want to understand how technology can be used to solve real-world customer and business problems.

During the internship, participants will learn how to design and architect solutions using the AWS Cloud while developing both technical and interpersonal skills.

Interns will work alongside experienced AWS professionals and receive guidance as they learn how to approach cloud architecture, customer engagement, and technology implementation.

The program combines:

  • Technical training
  • Mentorship
  • Cloud computing education
  • Customer engagement
  • Hands-on projects
  • Software and architecture development
  • Professional development

What Will You Learn?

The internship’s three-month mentorship program is designed to help participants develop practical Solutions Architect skills.

Participants will:

  1. Learn how to architect solutions on AWS.
  2. Develop skills for leading customer engagements.
  3. Work alongside experienced Solutions Architects and other professionals.
  4. Gain practical experience with AWS services.
  5. Learn how to translate customer problems into technical requirements.
  6. Develop technical and business knowledge.
  7. Gain experience communicating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

As a Solutions Architect Intern, you may be responsible for helping develop solutions to customer problems and supporting the adoption of AWS services.

Designing Solutions

Interns will work on solutions that address customer business challenges and help customers adopt AWS technologies.

This means understanding the customer’s needs and considering how AWS services can be combined to create an appropriate technical solution.

Working With Customers

The role involves interaction with both internal and external customers.

You may communicate with:

  • Developers
  • Technical teams
  • Team leads
  • Business stakeholders
  • Other AWS professionals

Strong communication and interpersonal skills are therefore an important part of the position.

Translating Customer Feedback

Interns will also learn how to gather useful feedback from customers and transform that feedback into clear:

  • Business requirements
  • Technical requirements
  • Product requirements
  • Engineering requirements

This helps connect customer needs with the teams responsible for developing products and technical solutions.

What Does a Typical Internship Day Look Like?

The internship is designed around practical experience rather than only classroom learning.

During the program, interns may:

Work on Real Business Challenges

Participants can engage directly with actual business problems and learn how technology can be used to address them.

Build on AWS

Interns gain hands-on experience working with the AWS Cloud and applying AWS services to practical situations.

Apply Architecture Best Practices

Participants will learn how established cloud architecture principles can be applied when designing solutions.

Solve Customer Problems

The program emphasizes working backwards from customer needs.

Rather than simply starting with a technology and looking for somewhere to use it, interns learn to understand the problem first and then develop an appropriate solution.

Work With Mentors

Interns work with experienced professionals who provide guidance throughout the program.

This mentorship is intended to help participants develop the skills required for customer-facing technical roles.

About the AWS Emerging Talent Team

The internship is part of the Emerging Talent team within AWS Industries and Strategic Accounts.

The team focuses on developing the next generation of professionals for roles such as:

  • Solutions Architects
  • Customer Solutions Managers
  • Sales professionals

These professionals work with some of AWS’s large and influential customers across different industries.

The team uses a cohort-based approach to talent development, providing participants with resources such as:

  • Education
  • Mentorship
  • Job-shadowing opportunities
  • Practical experience

The objective is to help emerging talent develop the skills needed to work in customer-facing roles.

Basic Qualifications

Applicants must meet the basic requirements specified for the position.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

18 years of age or older.

Education

Applicants must currently be enrolled in a:

  • Bachelor’s degree program, or
  • Higher degree program

The degree must be in:

  • Computer Science
  • Computer Engineering
  • A related technical field

Applicants are expected to graduate between:

December 2027 and September 2028.

Internship Commitment

Applicants must be able to:

  • Work 40 hours per week
  • Commit to the full 12-week internship

The position is a full-time internship.

Programming Experience

Applicants need experience with at least one of the following programming languages:

  • Java
  • Python
  • Node.js
  • C#
  • C++

Experience may come from academic work, projects, internships, or other relevant technical experiences, provided it meets the employer’s requirements.

Technical Experience

Applicants must have experience in at least one of the following technical domains:

  • Analytics
  • Security
  • Storage
  • DevOps
  • Application development
  • Machine learning

The position therefore targets students who already have some technical foundation rather than applicants with no technical experience.

Generative AI and Machine Learning

The position also specifically lists experience with emerging technologies such as:

  • Generative AI
  • Large Language Models (LLMs)
  • Machine Learning (ML)

Students who have worked with these technologies through coursework, projects, research, internships, or other relevant experiences may find this requirement particularly relevant to their background.

Customer Service and Communication Skills

Technical ability is only one part of the role.

Applicants are also expected to have experience demonstrating:

  • Customer service
  • Communication
  • Interpersonal skills

This reflects the customer-facing nature of a Solutions Architect position.

Solutions Architects need to communicate technical concepts to customers and collaborate with different teams, so the ability to work effectively with people is an important part of the internship.

Preferred Qualifications

Amazon also identifies several qualifications that can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

AWS Certification

An AWS certification is preferred.

Although it is listed as a preferred qualification rather than a basic requirement, applicants with relevant AWS certifications may be able to demonstrate additional familiarity with AWS technologies and cloud concepts.

Communicating Complex Ideas

Applicants who have experience communicating complex technical concepts to both:

  • Technical audiences
  • Non-technical audiences

are preferred.

This could include explaining technical projects to classmates, customers, managers, judges, or other stakeholders.

Frameworks and Design Patterns

Amazon also prefers candidates who have experience applying established:

  • Frameworks
  • Design patterns
  • Software development approaches

to produce working software.

This experience can come from:

  • University coursework
  • Personal projects
  • Hackathons
  • Previous internships

Location

The internship is available in two locations:

Dallas, Texas

The position is available in Dallas, TX.

Seattle, Washington

The position is also available in Seattle, WA.

Applicants should consider the location requirements when applying because the internship is described as an onsite role.

Work Schedule

Amazon states that its internships are full-time positions.

Interns should expect to work:

Monday through Friday

for up to:

40 hours per week

The internship lasts:

12 consecutive weeks.

The typical working hours are described as approximately 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Cohort-Based Start Dates

This is a cohort-based program, meaning participants are expected to begin together.

The supplied job description lists tentative start dates of:

  • May 24
  • June 21

Applicants should confirm the applicable start date during the recruitment process.

APPLY HERE

Salary Information

The supplied listing states a starting annualized pay figure of:

$103,275 USD annually for Dallas, Texas.

Because this is an internship, applicants should confirm how compensation is applied to the internship period and whether the amount varies by location or other factors.

Amazon Benefits and Support

The job listing states that Amazon provides several benefits beginning on the first day of employment, including:

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Mental Health Support
  • Medical Advice Line
  • 401(k) matching

Benefits and eligibility can depend on applicable employment terms and location.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

Amazon states that it is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Applicants who have a disability and require an accommodation or adjustment during the application or hiring process can request support.

How to Prepare for This Internship

Students interested in the Solutions Architect Intern position can strengthen their preparation by developing experience across both technical and communication areas.

1. Build Cloud Computing Knowledge

Learn the fundamentals of cloud computing and become familiar with AWS services and architecture concepts.

2. Develop Programming Skills

Gain practical experience in at least one of the programming languages listed by Amazon:

  • Python
  • Java
  • Node.js
  • C#
  • C++

3. Work on Personal Projects

Personal technical projects can help demonstrate your ability to turn concepts into working applications.

Projects involving cloud computing, AI, machine learning, data, security, or software development can be particularly relevant.

4. Participate in Hackathons

Amazon specifically identifies hackathons as one way candidates may gain experience applying frameworks and design patterns to working software.

5. Learn Generative AI and LLMs

Since the job description specifically mentions Generative AI, LLMs, and ML, students can develop familiarity with these technologies through coursework, projects, or practical experimentation.

6. Improve Communication Skills

Practice explaining technical concepts in simple language.

A Solutions Architect needs to communicate with people who may have very different levels of technical knowledge.

7. Consider an AWS Certification

An AWS certification is listed as a preferred qualification.

Students interested in the role may therefore consider learning about AWS certification pathways and determining which certification aligns with their existing experience.

Learn more HERE

or HERE

Who Is This Internship Suitable For?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to university students studying technical disciplines who are interested in combining:

  • Cloud computing
  • Software development
  • Technology consulting
  • Customer engagement
  • Solutions architecture
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • DevOps
  • Data and analytics

The position is especially focused on developing future customer-facing technical professionals.

Application Information

Job Title: Solutions Architect Intern, AWSI – 2027

Job ID: 10550494

Applicants should search for Job ID 10550494 on Amazon’s official careers platform to locate the current application listing.

The supplied information does not provide a specific application deadline. Because internship recruitment timelines can vary, applicants should check the official Amazon Jobs listing for the current application status and closing date.

Conclusion

The Amazon Web Services Solutions Architect Intern – 2027 program offers a 12-week, full-time opportunity for students pursuing computer science, computer engineering, or related technical degrees.

The program combines AWS technical training, mentorship, hands-on cloud experience, customer interaction, and practical problem-solving. Interns can work on real business challenges while learning how Solutions Architects design cloud-based solutions and translate customer requirements into technical solutions.

Applicants need to be at least 18 years old, enrolled in an eligible technical degree program, graduating between December 2027 and September 2028, and able to commit to the full 12-week, 40-hour-per-week internship. Experience with programming, cloud-related technical domains, and Generative AI, LLMs, or machine learning is also required according to the listing.

The internship is based in Dallas, Texas or Seattle, Washington, making it an opportunity for students seeking practical experience within AWS’s customer-facing technology environment.

For more information click HERE

item.content:encoded:
The CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 is now accepting applications from qualified candidates interested in pursuing doctoral research in agricultural sciences and related interdisciplinary fields at a German university. The scholarship provides an opportunity for researchers with an MSc degree to develop a PhD project connected to ongoing CGIAR++ research activities and to work under joint supervision from a senior CGIAR++ scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university.

For the 2026 call, the Hub plans to support 10 PhD candidates. The previous call in 2025 attracted a high volume of qualified applications and had an acceptance rate of just 5%, highlighting the competitive nature of the opportunity.

The application deadline for the current call is 30 November 2026.

CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 Overview

The programme is designed for candidates who want to undertake doctoral research that contributes to existing CGIAR++ research activities. A particularly important feature of the scholarship is its collaborative structure: applicants cannot apply independently without first establishing the required academic and research partnerships.

Each accepted candidate must form a “tridem” consisting of:

  1. The PhD candidate.
  2. A senior CGIAR++ scientist.
  3. A professor affiliated with a German university.

These three parties are expected to work together to develop the scientific proposal and establish the supervision and research arrangements required for the PhD.

The PhD project must also be connected to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity and should provide additional value to that research programme.

Deadline for the CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026

Application deadline: 30 November 2026

Applicants should begin preparing their applications well before the deadline because the process requires coordination with both a CGIAR++ senior scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university.

The required supervisory and hosting documents must also be prepared and submitted according to the application instructions.

Who Can Apply for the CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship?

The call is aimed at candidates who already hold an MSc degree in Agricultural Sciences or a related discipline and who meet the academic requirements specified by the programme.

Relevant academic backgrounds can include a broad range of disciplines, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature of the research supported by the programme.

Examples specifically listed in the call include:

  • Agricultural Sciences
  • Biology
  • Geography
  • Sociology
  • Veterinary Medicine
  • Marine Biology
  • Forestry
  • Political Sciences
  • Law
  • Economics
  • Other related fields

Applicants are expected to have achieved an above-average final grade in their MSc degree.

Requirements for Non-European Degrees

Candidates holding degrees from outside Europe must additionally provide a ranking from the issuing university.

This requirement allows the programme to assess the academic standing of qualifications obtained outside the European university system.

A Unique Three-Way Research and Supervision Structure

One of the most important requirements of the scholarship is that applicants must establish the appropriate research partnership before submitting their application.

Only applications from the required “tridems” will be accepted.

The tridem consists of:

1. The PhD Candidate

The candidate develops and undertakes the proposed doctoral research and must meet the academic requirements of the programme.

2. CGIAR++ Senior Scientist

The candidate must work with a senior scientist from a CGIAR++ Center. The scientist serves as the CGIAR++ supervisor and must confirm the candidate’s connection to an appropriate CGIAR++ research programme or project.

3. Professor at a German University

The candidate must also identify a professor affiliated with a German university who will jointly supervise the doctoral project.

The scientific proposal is developed collaboratively by these three parties.

This means prospective applicants should not wait until the final stages of the application process to identify their supervisors. Establishing the required research relationships is an essential part of becoming eligible to apply.

PhD Research Must Be Connected to CGIAR++ Research

Another central requirement is that candidates must be hosted by a CGIAR++ Center.

The proposed doctoral research must be attached to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity.

The call indicates that the project is preferably connected to an international, multidisciplinary research project.

The proposed PhD research should not simply duplicate existing research. Instead, it should be:

  • Connected to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity.
  • Complementary to the existing research.
  • Designed to provide additional value to the CGIAR++ research activity.
  • Supported by an appropriate CGIAR++ Center.
  • Developed with the CGIAR++ and German university supervisors.

This makes the scholarship particularly relevant to candidates who can demonstrate how their proposed doctoral research fits into a broader research programme.

PhD Study at a German University

Successful candidates must enroll in a PhD study programme at a German university.

However, applicants do not need to be German nationals.

The programme therefore provides an opportunity for qualified international candidates to pursue doctoral studies in Germany while maintaining a research connection with a CGIAR++ Center.

Applicants from CGIAR++ partner countries are welcome to apply.

The call also specifically states that female students are particularly encouraged to apply.

Documents Required from Applicants

Candidates must prepare several documents as part of their application.

1. Letter of Motivation

Applicants must provide a signed letter of motivation.

The letter must be:

  • Signed by the applicant.
  • No more than one page.

The motivation letter should be prepared carefully because it forms part of the candidate’s application package.

2. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a tabular CV.

The CV must be:

  • No more than one page.
  • Signed.
  • Dated.
  • Presented in tabular form.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their CV follows the format requested by the programme rather than submitting an unnecessarily long academic CV.

3. Research Proposal

A research proposal is required.

Applicants must use the official research proposal template provided by the programme.

Research Proposal Template

The proposal should be developed jointly with the required supervisors because the scholarship specifically requires a scientific proposal created through the tridem structure.

4. MSc Certificate and Academic Transcript

Applicants must submit:

  • Their MSc certificate.
  • Their transcript of academic records.

These documents must be issued by the examination office.

Applicants with non-European degrees should also remember the additional requirement concerning university ranking.

5. English Proficiency Certificate

Applicants must provide evidence of English-language proficiency.

The call accepts:

  • TOEFL
  • IELTS
  • Another English proficiency certificate

Candidates should make sure that their proof of English proficiency satisfies the programme’s requirements.

Documents Required From the Supervisors

The application also requires documents from the two supervisory sides of the proposed PhD.

These documents must be sent by the respective supervisors as one PDF by email to:

hub@landscapealliance.org

The supervisor documentation includes three important components.

1. German University Professor’s Recommendation and Supervision Confirmation

The professor affiliated with a German university must provide:

  • A letter of recommendation.
  • Confirmation of supervision.

The programme provides a specific template that should be used.

German University Supervisor Template

2. CGIAR++ Scientist Recommendation and Supervision Commitment

This makes the opportunity highly selective, particularly considering the programme’s previous application experience.

According to the information provided in the call, the 2025 application round attracted a high volume of qualified applications and had an acceptance rate of 5%.

Prospective applicants should therefore pay close attention to the eligibility requirements, research proposal, supervisory arrangements and supporting documentation.

What Makes the Research Opportunity Interdisciplinary?

Applicants may come from fields including:

  • Biology
  • Geography
  • Sociology
  • Veterinary Medicine
  • Marine Biology
  • Forestry

  • Law

This interdisciplinary approach can be particularly relevant for research addressing complex agricultural, environmental, social, economic, governance or development-related questions.

The requirement for the PhD project to complement ongoing CGIAR++ research also means that applicants should consider how their research connects with broader research activities rather than developing an isolated doctoral project.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because applicants must establish relationships with both a CGIAR++ scientist and a German university professor, preparation should begin early.

Step 1: Confirm Your Academic Eligibility

First, verify that you have an MSc degree in Agricultural Sciences or an appropriate related field and that your final grade is above average.

If your degree was awarded outside Europe, prepare the required university ranking documentation.

Step 2: Identify Potential Supervisors

You will need both:

  • A senior CGIAR++ scientist.
  • A professor affiliated with a German university.

The two supervisors must be able to jointly support the proposed PhD project.

Step 3: Develop the Research Idea

The research idea should be developed collaboratively with the supervisors.

Consider how the proposed research:

  • Fits into existing CGIAR++ research.
  • Complements ongoing work.
  • Adds value to the research programme.
  • Can be undertaken through a German university PhD programme.
  • Benefits from the expertise and research environment of the CGIAR++ Center.

Step 4: Prepare the Research Proposal

Use the official template rather than creating an unrelated format.

Because the proposal is central to the application, applicants should ensure that the proposed research is clearly connected to the ongoing CGIAR++ activity identified by the supervisors.

Step 5: Collect Academic Documents

Prepare your:

  • MSc certificate.
  • Academic transcript.
  • University ranking, if applicable.
  • English proficiency certificate.

Step 6: Prepare the Personal Documents

The motivation letter and CV must comply with the specified format.

The motivation letter has a maximum length of one page, while the CV must also be no more than one page and must be signed and dated.

Step 7: Coordinate the Supervisor Documents

The German university professor and CGIAR++ scientist must complete their respective documents, while the CGIAR++ Center must provide the Hosting Agreement.

These documents must be combined into one PDF and sent by the supervisors to hub@landscapealliance.org.

30 November 2026

Conclusion

The CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 provides an opportunity for qualified MSc graduates to pursue doctoral research at a German university while becoming part of an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity. Its interdisciplinary eligibility criteria make the programme relevant to applicants from agricultural sciences as well as fields such as biology, geography, sociology, forestry, veterinary medicine, political sciences, law and economics.

A distinctive feature of the opportunity is its required tridem structure, bringing together the PhD candidate, a senior CGIAR++ scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university. The proposed doctoral research must also be connected to an existing CGIAR++ research programme and demonstrate additional value to that work.

With only 10 PhD candidates being supported in the current call and a reported 5% acceptance rate in the 2025 call, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements, research proposal and supervisory documentation.

Are you passionate about world development and are looking for valuable experiences to complement your studies? The UNDP Internship Program is an outstanding opportunity where interns have the chance to learn about the leading development programs initiated by the United Nations. The UNDP Internship program  aims to provide candidates interested in international development with a deeper knowledge of the UNDP’s work. The UNDP Internship is an excellent opportunity for individuals who are interested in hands-on experience with issues related to global poverty eradication and sustainable development.

UNDP offers attractive paid positions in several areas for the sole purpose of promoting global development. Around 170 countries are part of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), which is the leading development promotion agency of the UN. UNDP interns have a tremendous opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience working with qualified, well-trained, and exceedingly experienced mentors and supervisors to achieve the goals of the UNDP. The organization works towards a better future for humanity by addressing issues such as eradicating poverty, reducing inequities and exclusion, and empowering countries to embark on sustainable development and growth.

The UNDP internship program includes students and recent graduates from the most diverse fields of knowledge. The most popular areas of study in this program are Economics, Public or Business Administration, Environmental Studies, International Relations, and Other related areas. The type of activities that interns perform can vary depending on the opening and the needs of the department where they are placed. The following are the most common responsibilities: Conducting research, Writing documents, Cataloguing information, forums, or other collaborative events, Assisting in the organization of conferences, and Publishing knowledge stories/best practices. These internships can take place at the UN’s headquarters, its country offices, or regional offices. The length of an internship depends on both the candidate’s qualifications and the needs of the UN. 

UNDP Internship Program Details:

  • Host Organization: United Nation Development Program
  • Program Locations: UNDP Country Offices, at Regional Hubs or Headquarters in New York.
  • Internship Type: Full-time/Part-time (Paid)
  • Eligible Countries: All
  • Deadline: Varies

What are the Benefits of the UNDP Internship Program?

  • The UNDP interns would receive a monthly stipend.
  • UNDP interns receive a monthly stipend to cover costs associated with the internship. Stipend amounts can vary from one duty station to another.
  • There are chances that interns will be assigned to UNDP or to the UN system in the future.
  • Additionally, interns may receive financial aid from their nominating institutions or the government.

Eligibility Criteria for the UNDP Internships:

  • Applicants from all over the world may apply for the UNDP internships.
  • Candidates can either be enrolled in a graduate program or have earned a second university degree, or they can be in the final academic year of their first university degree.
  • The candidate should have fluency in at least one of UNDP’s three working languages: French, English, and Spanish.
  • The knowledge of Arabic, Portuguese, Russian, or another Eastern European language would be advantageous.
  • The candidates should be able to demonstrate their relevance to UNDP programs.
  • At the time of application, the candidate must be at least 18 years of age.
  • The candidate must demonstrate the ability to work with people from different languages, national, and cultural backgrounds.

Deadline:

The application deadline to apply for the UNDP internship varies according to each internship program.

How to Apply for the UNDP Internship Program?

  • Candidates must submit their applications only via UNDP’s website.
  • Internship opportunities at UNDP are listed in the UNDP Job Section.
  • Please select an area of interest and then click “Apply.”.
  • Please ensure that you follow the specific deadline for the internship program, as each internship has a different and exclusive deadline.
  • If you wish to apply to more than one program, you must register separately for each program.
